messages:
alex: Quick question — for compact signer bundles (delta-first packaging) should operators be allowed to evict old signed artifacts before activation? We're hitting disk pressure on some on‑prem boxes. Thinking about safe eviction semantics + verifier continuity + a healthcheck/dry-run playbook.

maria: +1. We need to guarantee the verifier can still validate the currently active set. If we remove artifacts that are referenced by the activation manifest we break rollbacks. Keep an explicit retention list.

suhas: Proposal: add an `activation_window` object to manifests that lists minimal ancestor anchors that must be retained. Garbage collector can delete anything outside that window. Also record tombstones as signed attestations (so verifier can be confident deletion was deliberate).

jen: How does this interact with seedless bootstrap? If we evict seeds, nodes doing a fresh bootstrap might fail. We should ensure a tiny bootstrap bundle is preserved.

alex: Agreed. For seedless nodes allow eviction but require a tiny `bootstrap-bundle` (compressed index + anchor) stored in a separate retention tier (configurable path). Target size < 10MB.

nate: For safety add a pre-apply `verify-only` mode: verifier runs against candidate bundles and emits a signed `dry-run-ok` attestation. Garbage collector checks for that attestation before considering deletion of referenced blobs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: helper CLI exists: `rductl verify --bundle /path/to/bundle.tar --dry-run` which prints `attestation:sha256:<digest>` to stdout and appends to `/var/log/rdu/attestations.json`.

lucy: UX request: Console should show `eviction would orphan manifest #<n>` and require a manual bypass with justification (audit record). Otherwise operators might accidentally orphan active manifests.

maria: Tradeoff: retention increases storage footprint. We should autosuggest retention values by analyzing last successful bootstraps and activation windows (Redwood Optimize integration).

suhas: Also need an activation rollback flow: if verification fails during activation, pause and roll back to previous image. Implementation: snapshot activation marker and keep pre-apply KV until commit window closes.

jen: Drafted an eviction marker schema (example):
```
eviction_marker: {
  "artifact": "sha256:abcd...",
  "retain_until_activation": "2025-05-01T00:00:00Z",
  "signed_by": "operator-key-id"
}
```
This sits in the manifest and is signed by the operator key.

alex: Nice. To expose to customers: `rductl audit evict --since 24h` and Console -> Operations -> Evictions view. Also include per-eviction attestation link.

nate: Ops playbook note: when reclaiming disk prefer evicting large unreferenced layers and logs first (heuristic). Only evict model shard blobs when necessary and with explicit attestation.

lucy: I'll draft an RFC blurb with failure modes, CLI examples, console wireframes, and small test plan (dry-run, intentional corrupt blob, simulated low-disk). Target PR by EOW.

alex: Thanks — tagging @sre-team for rollout soak plan and verifying the `verify-only` attestation roundtrip. :thumbsup:

sre-team: ack — we'll run soak on 3 dedicated boxes and run 10k bootstrap replays from the test harness, report perf + failure modes.

alex: One more ops detail: GC should be staged: mark -> quarantine (48h) -> finalize; quarantine exposes blocked bootstraps via audit endpoint so we can revert quickly.

lucy: Good call. I'll include the staged GC timeline and an operator `gc revert <marker>` command in the RFC.

alex: Perfect. If no major objections I'll fold this into the on‑prem packaging RFC as a follow-up section.

maria: No objections from me.

suhas: LGTM, add tests for attestation verification that simulate key rotation.

alex: Cool — thanks everyone.
